title: Pointwise Wick-square coercivity for arbitrary Gaussian mean and local variance

local_coercivity.field_data: For b_N(x)_j=sqrt(lambda_j)e_j(x), a Gaussian N(m,S) has pointwise field mean h(x)=b_N(x)^T m and local centered variance v(x)=b_N(x)^T S b_N(x)>=0, with vacuum variance C_N=|b_N(x)|^2 constant
local_coercivity.mean_optimization: Minimizing over y=h^2>=0 gives f_C(v)=6v(2C-v) for 0<=v<=C and f_C(v)=3(v-C)^2+6C^2 for v>=C
local_coercivity.uniform_coercivity: For every v>=0, f_C(v)>=c_* C v with the sharp constant c_*=6(sqrt(3)-1); on 0<=v<=C use f_C/(Cv)=6(2-v/C), while on v>=C the minimum of 3(t-2+3/t) occurs at t=sqrt(3)
local_coercivity.spike_guard: The bound is pointwise and linear in v, so spatially varying covariance and arbitrarily concentrated local-variance spikes cannot evade it by averaging a concave branch
local_coercivity.integrated_consequence: Writing V_N=integral v(x)dx=Tr(Lambda S) in the orthonormal real Fourier basis, the interaction expectation is at least g c_* C_N V_N
local_coercivity.scope_guard: This is a Gaussian one-point-moment bound; it does not impose stationarity or diagonal covariance, but it does not extend to non-Gaussian fourth moments
